name: Founding and Core Beliefs

objectives.text: Identify Muslims as people who follow the religion of Islam
Recall that Muslims worship one god whom they call Allah
Identify Mecca in Arabia as the city where Islam began and the most holy city for Muslims
Explain that Christians also confess one God but confess this one God as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit
Summarize the main events of Muhammad's life including his claimed revelations, the Hijra to Medina, and his return to Mecca
Explain that the word Islam means submission and that a Muslim is understood as one who submits to Allah
Compare the Islamic view of Isa as a human prophet with the Bible's teaching that Jesus is the eternal Son of God made flesh
List the six articles of Islamic faith concerning Allah, angels, revealed books, prophets, the Day of Judgment, and divine decree
Describe the Islamic doctrine of tawhid and explain why Muslims regard belief in the Trinity as shirk
Distinguish what Genesis records about Ishmael from later Islamic and Arab traditions that link Abraham and Ishmael to Mecca
Explain how the early Muslim community spread under the first caliphs after Muhammad's death
Explain how the Sunni and Shia division arose from the dispute over succession after Muhammad and identify key differences between them
Analyze the Islamic claim that Muhammad is the seal of the prophets in light of the biblical teaching that God has spoken finally in his Son
Contrast the Islamic view of human nature and sin with the Reformed doctrine of original sin
Compare the Islamic hope of judgment by the weighing of deeds with the Reformed doctrine of justification by grace through faith
Evaluate the Islamic denial of Jesus' crucifixion using the New Testament eyewitness testimony and the Reformed teaching on why Christ's death was necessary
Evaluate the Islamic charge that the Trinity is polytheism using Scripture and the Reformed confession of one God in three persons
Develop a respectful explanation of the gospel that answers a core Islamic objection to Christian belief
Compose an argument comparing the Islamic emphasis on God's sovereign will with the Christian confession that God is love eternally within the Trinity

changes: Removed the Nicene Creed citations and anchored Trinity and Christology objectives to Westminster and Heidelberg references instead. Dropped mosque, prayer mats, Shahada, Bible corruption, and Gospel reliability objectives as belonging to the Five Pillars and Sacred Texts siblings. Kept and reworded Muslims, Allah, Mecca, Muhammad, submission, Isa, Ishmael, Sunni and Shia, crucifixion, Trinity, and nature of God objectives. Added six articles of faith, tawhid, early caliphate, seal of the prophets, sin and human nature, judgment versus justification, and respectful gospel engagement.
